page.layout: Two printed pages on one scan. Left page: one column of running text under the head "224" and running head "ΘΕ". Right page (facing page, partly cut off at the right edge): narrow columns of text with marginal glosses, read from top to bottom.

main_text.p: Θεομάχος ος ὁ ἡ Deo repugnans. ex μάχη ης η pugna, & Θεὸς Deus, Act.5.39.
Θεόπνευστος ὁ ἡ, divinitus inspiratus a. πνέω inspiratus, est à πνέω spiro, 2.Tim.3.16.
Θεοσεβὴς ἐς ὁ ἡ Dei cultor, trix. ex σέβομαι colo, veneror, & Θεὸς, Deus, Joh.9.31.
Θεοστυγὴς ἐς ὁ ἡ Dei osor. ex στυγέω odi & Θεὸς, vide supra ἀπο στυγέω, Rom.1.30.
Θεραπεία ας ἡ fanatio Luc.9. 11. famulitium Matth.24.45. sanitas Apoc.22.2.

Θεραπεύω proprie, famulor, servio. de ingenuis dicitur operam suam prompta quadam voluntate aliis navantibus. Per syn. gen. curo, sano cum Accus. imperf. ἐθεράπευον ες ε. Fut. θεραπεύσω. prat.act. τεθεράπευκα. a.1.act. ἐθεράπευσα. aor.1.imperat. θεράπευσον ἁπλῶς cura. praes.pass. θεραπεύομαι sanor, semel color Actor.17.25. imperf.pass. ἐθεραπευόμην & ετο Act.5.16. prat.pass. τεθεράπευμαι. part.prat. pass. τεθεραπευμένος η ον. a.1. pass. ἐθεραπεύθην ης η sanatus fui.
Θεράπων οντος ὁ minister, famulus, Heb.3.5. θεράπαινα ης ἡ famula.
Θερίζω meto cum Accus. sape absolute ponitur, Matth.6.26. Fut. ἰσω. P. τεθέρικα. a.1. ἐθέρισα messui. part.a.1. θερίσας αὐτὸς ὁ prat. pass. τεθέρισμαι. a.1. ἐθερίσθην.

page.notes: The Greek is printed in a cursive style with accents and breathings that I could not read with full certainty; the Greek words above are marked by their likely forms and may contain small errors. The right page is cut off at the right edge; its narrow column text and marginal glosses are only partly legible, so those fragments are not transcribed here. The Greek running head is read as printed. No stamps or shelf marks were transcribed.
